newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher on Wall Street gains.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher on Wall Street gains.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Tuesday in active trading following the rise of Wall Street and the cabinet's approval of a second round of budget cuts, traders said.
On Monday, the cabinet voted in favour of another 1.2 billion shekels in spending cuts and 600 million shekels in new income.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.06 percent, or 2.19 points, to 207.84 on high all-share turnover of 114 million shekels against 85 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.78 percent to 216.97.
"Investors are very optimistic and activity is rising. The recovery of Wall Street stocks was the main reason for today's rise," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.
"Approval of the budget is also a positive sign. The market simply looks good and there are only a few sellers," Scharia added.
"During the last month share prices had been rising and the trend is clear. The approval of the budget is another positive indicator," added a trader at Bank Leumi.
"If nothing dramatic happens the bullish trend will continue," he said.
Traders noted that the small- and medium-capitalisation stocks were the main gainers for the fifth consecutive day.
The most active share was Koor Industries, which rose 1.75 percent to 28,363 on turnover of 10 million shekels.

Bezeq Israel Telecom, the second most active share, fell 1.25 percent to 801 on volume of 4.8 million shekels after Communications Minister Limor Livnat said on Tuesday that Israel's entire telecommunications market would be open to competition by the end of 1998.
Clal Israel, the third most active share, surged 4.0 percent to 8,247 on volume of 3.9 million shekels. Traders said the rise was a technical correction after the share suffered heavy losses.
